steps.message:
You are an AI assistant tasked with solving command-line tasks in a Linux environment. You will be given a task description and the output from previously executed commands. Your goal is to solve the task by providing batches of shell commands.

Format your response as JSON with the following structure:

{
  "analysis": "Analyze the current state based on the terminal output provided. What do you see? What has been accomplished? What still needs to be done?",
  "plan": "Describe your plan for the next steps. What commands will you run and why? Be specific about what you expect each command to accomplish.",
  "commands": [
    {
      "keystrokes": "ls -la\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    },
    {
      "keystrokes": "cd project\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    }
  ],
  "task_complete": true
}

Required fields:
- "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation
- "plan": Your plan for the next steps
- "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:
- "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

Task Description:
Rivetbay on this bench turns event descriptions into field decoders. Descriptions live at `/app/rivetbay/evd/*.evd`. One mill pass must refresh `/app/rivetbay/intake/current.ledger` from those files and write one `/app/rivetbay/emitters/<name>.kdec` per description discovered on that run. `/app/bin/rivetbay mill` is that pass; `/app/bin/rivetbay decode <frame>` prints JSON for a sample under `/app/rivetbay/frames`. A description with no decoder decodes as unknown.

Some descriptions on disk currently finish mill without a matching `.kdec`, decode as unknown, and leave emitters short of the description set; mill must exit non-zero when decoders are fewer than descriptions. One mill subprocess must leave emitters equal to the descriptions present for that run, and decode of a newly added event must print its fields.

The C pipeline under `/app/rivetbay` drives `/app/bin/rivetbay` and must be corrected so mill regenerates the ledger and `.kdec` files; static or hand-placed ledger or decoder files are not enough. The verifier reruns `/app/bin/rivetbay mill` and `/app/bin/rivetbay decode` on fresh descriptions and frames. Ledger lines are `name|relpath|field:kind,...` with kinds `u8` and `u16` in description order. Each `.kdec` starts with `KDEC1`, then `NAME <name>`, then one `field kind` line per field. Decode JSON is `{"kind":"decoded","name":"<name>","fields":{...}}` with integer field keys from the description (such as mm, latch, force, amp, bit, thick, q, n, and w), or `{"kind":"unknown","name":"<name>"}` when no decoder exists. Frame bytes are a 4-byte big-endian name length, the name, then packed big-endian field payloads.

steps.message:
Analysis: The defect is confirmed: driver.c snapshots the old ledger with prime_intake_sheet(), discovery rewrites the on-disk ledger, but emit_all() still consumes the stale in-memory snapshot. Thus galley_hatch enters the ledger but gets no decoder, and count_gap incorrectly compares the seven stale sheet lines with seven emitters and returns success. Mill must load the newly discovered ledger before emission. Also, emit_all currently never removes stale .kdec files, so emitters cannot equal the descriptions present on a run after a description is removed.
Plan: Change the mill sequence to discover first and then grab the refreshed ledger into memory. Update emission to remove existing .kdec files before generating the current set, ensuring exact synchronization. Rebuild the binary, run mill, verify its status and artifact set, and decode galley_hatch.

arguments.keystrokes:
python3 - <<'PY'
p='/app/rivetbay/forgekit/driver.c'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('        prime_intake_sheet();\n        discover_all();\n        pour_sheet();', '        discover_all();\n        grab_sheet();\n        pour_sheet();')
open(p,'w').write(s)
PY

/app/bin/rivetbay mill; rc=$?; echo "mill_rc=$rc"; echo '--- ledger'; cat /app/rivetbay/intake/current.ledger; echo '--- emitters'; find /app/rivetbay/emitters -maxdepth 1 -name '*.kdec' -printf '%f\n' | sort; echo '--- galley decoder'; cat /app/rivetbay/emitters/galley_hatch.kdec; echo '--- decode'; /app/bin/rivetbay decode /app/rivetbay/frames/galley_hatch.bin

steps.message:
Analysis: The rebuilt pipeline now refreshes the in-memory sheet after discovery, creates galley_hatch.kdec, keeps eight emitters for eight descriptions, exits successfully, and decodes galley_hatch correctly. Stale .kdec cleanup was also added. We should validate the verifier's key scenario: add a brand-new description and frame, mill once, decode it, then remove the description and confirm the next single mill removes its stale emitter. Finally, inspect source changes and run all existing frame decodes.
Plan: Create a temporary valid event with u16 and u8 fields and a correctly packed frame. Run one mill and decode it, checking ledger/emitter counts. Remove the temporary description and frame, run one mill again, and verify its decoder is removed and counts return to eight. Then decode every existing frame and show the final source diff.

PY

rm -f /app/rivetbay/evd/verifier_probe.evd /app/rivetbay/frames/verifier_probe.bin
/app/bin/rivetbay mill; rc=$?; echo "remove_mill_rc=$rc"; test ! -e /app/rivetbay/emitters/verifier_probe.kdec && echo 'stale_probe_removed=yes'; echo "evd=$(find /app/rivetbay/evd -maxdepth 1 -name '*.evd' | wc -l) ledger=$(grep -cve '^[[:space:]]*$' /app/rivetbay/intake/current.ledger) kdec=$(find /app/rivetbay/emitters -maxdepth 1 -name '*.kdec' | wc -l)"

set -e; for f in /app/rivetbay/frames/*.bin; do printf '%s: ' "$(basename "$f")"; /app/bin/rivetbay decode "$f"; done; echo '--- changed sources'; grep -n -A8 -B3 'discover_all' /app/rivetbay/forgekit/driver.c; grep -n -A35 -B3 'clear_emitters' /app/rivetbay/forgekit/emit.c
